subject: psychology
title: Biopsychology: Plasticity & Functional Recovery
welcome_lead: The brain rewires after injury — sometimes spectacularly.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology plasticity and functional recovery: Maguire taxi drivers, Draganski.
final_note: Use it or lose it — and after damage, the spared brain takes up the slack.

concepts.def: Brain's ability to change physically with experience.
Removal of unused synaptic connections during development.
Surviving neurons grow new branches to replace lost ones.
Spared areas take over functions of damaged ones.
Education and stimulation buffer against decline.

walkthroughs.body_html: Maguire et al. (2000) scanned 16 London taxi drivers and found significantly larger posterior hippocampi than controls — and size correlated with years driving. Knowledge of London's streets physically reshapes the brain.

Draganski et al. (2006) scanned medical students before and after exams. Posterior parietal cortex grey matter increased after three months of revision. Plasticity isn't limited to childhood — adult brains restructure with practice.

After damage the brain recruits unused neurons via axonal sprouting, reformation of blood vessels and recruitment of homologous areas on the other hemisphere. Spontaneous recovery slows after a few weeks; constraint-induced therapy and rehabilitation extend gains.
